name: Cost
definition: Price, bill size or total cost of ownership drives the choice to adopt, leave or look elsewhere.
example_1_quote: But instead of moving to the cloud (and Databricks), they saved 5X costs by building their own analytics platform with Iceberg, Trino and Superset.
example_2_quote: The primary driver of inflated Snowflake bills for bursty, interactive workloads is the platform's billing model for compute.

name: Performance and scale
definition: Query speed, throughput or ability to handle growing data volume drives the choice.
example_1_quote: The DW got replaced with bigquery when we started doing more tracking.
example_2_quote: The total time for BigQuery to load 350GB of csv, run 12 different regular expressions against each, and output that to a new csv was about 10 minutes.

name: Right-sizing (platform is overkill)
definition: The workload is too small or too simple for a warehouse or lakehouse; a smaller tool such as Postgres is judged enough.
example_1_quote: In fact, I just advised someone recently to simply use Postgres instead of BigQuery since they had <1TB and their queries weren't super intensive.
example_2_quote: During the big data hype, I did a feasibility study for this for my previous company (typical bigcorp) and learned that most companies should not have a data lake.

name: Lock-in and openness
definition: Proprietary formats, runtimes or feature boundaries versus open formats and portability drive the choice.
example_1_quote: Those are managed platforms with their own runtimes and billing; EMR keeps you on open-source engines and open table formats you can lift to any other environment, at the cost of more assembly.
example_2_quote: It's all open, so this is only a half issue, but there are switching costs.

name: Operational simplicity and control
definition: How easy the platform is to run and use: managed versus fragmented services, user friendliness, and visibility into what it does.
example_1_quote: Trying to just run a simple Spark query using an S3 Table Bucket was enough to remind me why Snowflake and Databricks are printing money by making it a more user friendly experience.
example_2_quote: Frankly the entire analytics space on AWS feels like a huge mess of competing teams and products instead of a uniform vision.

name: Governance and security
definition: Access control, data-leak risk or a single governance model drives the choice.
example_1_quote: The best thing I've built in a long time is replacing a complex (and scary) permissions system built on top of Snowflake with single role duckdb databases that - aside from no longer worrying about bugs leaking data across roles - are more performant, timely and flexible.
example_2_quote: The zero-copy savings are nice; the governance simplification is what will actually convince your security org to let you retire the export jobs.

name: Ecosystem and integration fit
definition: Fit with the stack already in place (cloud, identity, BI tools, storage) or what integrates cleanly drives the choice.
example_1_quote: Fabric wins on Microsoft-shop fit because the identity, licensing, and Power BI story compound; Databricks wins on ML depth and cross-cloud reach; Snowflake wins on pure warehouse UX and Iceberg-native storage; Synapse is the legacy option that Fabric is actively replacing.
example_2_quote: If zero-copy is a requirement, evaluate AWS-native engines that authorise in the caller's own IAM context alongside it

name: Team skills and operating model
definition: The team's existing skills, or who on the team should own and operate the platform, drives the choice.
example_1_quote: I could use Java, but I am also managing our team and we want to stay with Python since that is our team's core skill set (myself included).
example_2_quote: and that is a team-and-cost question, not a file-format one.

name: Other stated reason
definition: A platform-choice reason is stated but fits none of the categories.
example_1_quote: Came here to say that Big Query is a phenomenal product, that alone is a reason for a lot of companies to adopt GCP.

name: No stated reason
definition: The document states no reason for choosing, leaving or evaluating a platform (how-to questions, job posts, news, or a switching phrase used in another sense).
example_1_quote: It generates pages that ignore your components, skip your tokens, and treat every screen like a fresh snowflake.
example_2_quote: I am trying to write a regex that can replace '[', ']' and '].' with '_' and in cases where ']' is the last character it should be replaced with '' but I am struggling to come up with a regex for it that works in all cases because Snowflake does not support lookahead & lookbehind.
